status: Concept proposal only; not an implemented level or approved asset
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a single wide 16:9 game-screen concept proposal for the next tomb dungeon area of an existing medieval math roguelite.
REFERENCE IMAGE: the attached approved concept is the binding art direction for ink, paper, character proportions, eye treatment, colour and engraved numbers. Change the camera and environment, not the visual language. This is NOT a realistic 3D dungeon and NOT modern painted fantasy.

Primary request: a FIRST-PERSON view walking into a medieval tomb passage. The player sees down the tunnel and meets enemies facing the camera; their own party is represented only by four portraits. Recreate the magic and tactile clarity of the reference as an old printed book illustration. A dramatic perspective change within the same game.

Composition: landscape wide screen. Upper approximately 72% is the explorable tunnel. A strong, readable one-point perspective down three receding irregular stone arches. Large worn stone blocks at the left and right frame the shot; distant arch and crooked closed door near the centre. Sparse shallow burial niches, a cracked stone coffin at one side, modest roots slipping between stones. Broad quiet areas between clusters of engraved detail; open pale paving in the foreground leads the eye into the scene. A single shabby skeletal tomb sentry in broken medieval armour faces the player near the middle distance, with a rusted sword and small battered shield, absurdly ill-fitting helmet and ragged dirty orange tabard. Full enemy silhouette visible, clear against the tunnel, not looming across the whole image. Slight spooky comedy, no gore or body horror. Small torch flames only as flat dirty-orange ink shapes, no glow or digitally lit walls.

At the very bottom of the world illustration, four small square portrait medallions in a tidy centred row, clearly inset HUD portraits, not physical people standing in the corridor: approved bucket-helmet knight; lean priest with orange hood up; strange human dark wizard with battered black pointed hat, not a demon; chainmail-coif firestarter. Human eyes are small shaded brow sockets with tiny paper-white glints, no big cartoon eyeballs. Portraits have restrained broken engraved borders, tiny two-heart indicators under each. Keep them compact enough that the corridor remains the dominant image. Do not add names or verbose labels.

Across the screen below the portrait row: the same thin worn horizontal ink divider from the approved concept, a tiny dirty orange diamond exactly at centre. This also serves as the timing track: compact shield icon around one quarter, flaming sword at halfway, plain sword at three quarters, stick near the far right. A short dull orange filled segment from the left, no neon. Under this divider the same light parchment continues seamlessly. One very clear large carved math problem centred, reading exactly "8 + 6 = ?" in the ornate engraved numeral style of the reference, with generous negative space. No action cards, no other buttons, no title or subtitles, no watermark.

Style: irregular black medieval woodblock edges with carved fine hatching and worn print breaks. Flat paper interiors, charcoal black and grey ink, muted parchment and a little old dirty orange. Match reference lineweight, dense detailed characters but airy environment, no overworked wall textures. Build darkness from deliberate solid black recesses and printed crosshatching, not gradients or a brown/black screen-wide tint. Walls, floor, skin and UI share the reference neutral aged parchment instead of yellow stone. All in one harmonious illustrated book page. Avoid painted lighting, glossy surfaces, plastic faces, modern fantasy rendering, huge UI panels, top-down maps, side-view party sprites, bones growing from walls, faces on bodies.
